children: Raw sugar futures on ICE steadied on Tuesday as the market continued to consolidate after hitting 16-month peaks last week, while arabica coffee hit a fresh 5-week low.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
settled up 0.03 cent, or 0.2%, at 18.10 cents per lb, having hit 18.77 cents last Wednesday.
* "Physical activity staying this thin looks more like a market pausing to digest the rally than one confirming it," said physical broker Deepcore.

* The broker said it is bearish near term at these price levels as current stocks are ample, adding that while the El Nino weather pattern remains a structural upside risk into 2027, it is "a slow-burn" factor.
* Rains in Brazil, meanwhile, are likely to hamper sugarcane harvesting with about a third of the crop still to be processed.

* Crude oil prices hit multi-week highs near $100 a barrel, limiting losses in sugar as higher energy prices tend to prompt cane mills in Brazil and India to produce less sugar and more ethanol, a cane-based biofuel.
* White sugar
fell 1.2% to $519.80 a metric ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 4.3 cents, or 1.5%, at $2.913 per lb, having hit a five-week low of $2.8660.

* Coffee is under pressure from an expected bumper 2026/27 crop in top grower Brazil, as well as for good climate conditions for the upcoming flowering stage that will set up the country's next year crop.
* Brazil exported 45% more coffee in August than in the same month a year ago.
* "The (bearish arabica) story seems to be picking up momentum now and is seemingly more believable," said a dealer.
* On the supporting side, arabica certified stocks hit a fresh 26-year low on ICE, although some coffee is showing up for grading.
* Robusta coffee
rose 1.6% to $3,458 a ton, having hit a 2-1/2-month low last week.
COCOA
* London cocoa
settled down £224, or 5%, to £4,295  per ton, some way off last Tuesday's one-year high of £4,988.
* El Nino is a worry for cocoa. But those concerns have lessened somewhat as, so far, the weather pattern has not brought excess rains to West Africa.
* New York cocoa
fell 4.4% to $5,913 a ton.
